title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page finishes a construction begun on the previous page. Its goal is a model of the space SP^Y_G (indexed by a graph or configuration G and a symmetric configuration Y = Y_Q) as an explicit principal homogeneous space under a real torus U^Â, where U is the unit circle. The model is chosen so that it carries a canonical finite set of base points. That finite set is then used to define the discrete 'special' Teichmüller groupoid S_0T^Q_G.

Setup from the previous page:
- The index set Â of edges or arcs splits as Â = Â_1 ⊔ J_I ⊔ J_II ⊔ J_III, according to how the symmetry of Y acts.
- Each factor T^Y_a is a circle-torsor of the form U ∧^{±1} E_a, where E_a is a two-element {±1}-torsor. These are orientation or 'half-twist' choices built from ω_Q (orientation torsor) and from the torsors J̃_{III,i}.
- For J_I ≠ ∅, the previous page sets E_{G,Q} = E_{Â_1} × ω_Q × E_{J_III}. This is a torsor under γ_G = {±1}^{Â_1} × {±1} × {±1}^{J_III}.

How γ_G maps into U^Â (this page):
- On Â_1 and J_III, {±1}^X → U^X is the evident coordinatewise inclusion.
- The single {±1} goes diagonally into U^{J_I}, i.e. through {±1} → {±1}^{J_I} → U^{J_I}.
- The J_II factors are already canonically trivialized as U, so γ_G contributes nothing there.

Result: SP^Y_G ≅ U^Â ∧^{γ_G} E_{G,Q}. This is the contracted product, i.e. the pushforward of a finite 2-group torsor along a homomorphism into a compact torus. It gives SP^Y_G as a U^Â-torsor together with a canonical γ_G-equivariant map E_{G,Q} → SP^Y_G.

When J_I = ∅:
- The factor ω_Q can be dropped, so E_{G,Q} = E_{Â_1} × E_{J_III}.
- Then γ_G = {±1}^{Â_1 ⊔ J_III}, and the same formula holds.

Definition of the groupoid: S_0T^Q_G = S_0T^{Y_Q}_G is the full subgroupoid of the fundamental groupoid Π_1(SP^Y_G) on the object set E_{G,Q}.
- Since SP^Y_G is a torus-torsor, each vertex group is Z^Â.
- Arrows between distinct base points are paths along the circle factors between the sign choices: half-turns, which square to full Dehn-twist-like loops.
- Grothendieck announces an explicit presentation by generators and relations ('j'y reviendrai'). The next page moves on to exceptional Y with an order-3 isotropy, where μ_3-torsors replace the ±1-torsors.

Modern reading: this is the torus of twist angles at a maximally degenerate, symmetric stable curve or cell. It is equipped with a finite 2-torsor of 'real' or tangential base points. The groupoid is the local Teichmüller groupoid at that point, with finitely many base points chosen canonically through symmetry.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The arrow written γ_G ↪ U^Â is injective only because the J_II part receives nothing and the diagonal {±1} → U^{J_I} is injective when J_I ≠ ∅. This is consistent with the text.

The phrase 'on peut poser pour simplifier' in the J_I = ∅ case presupposes that ω_Q plays no role there. This is plausible, since the T_{J_I} factors are the only ones twisted by ω_Q alone, but it is not argued on this page.

ideas.what: Presenting a torus-torsor as the contracted product U^Â ∧^{γ} E of a finite elementary 2-group torsor pushed along γ → U^Â, to obtain canonical finite base-point sets
ideas.modern_name: pushout of torsors / reduction of structure group of a torus-torsor to a finite subgroup; discrete base points on Fenchel–Nielsen twist tori
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard torsor formalism (Giraud, SGA); in the Teichmüller setting, cf. Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura–Schneps, Bakalov–Kirillov

ideas.what: Defining the Teichmüller-type groupoid S_0T^Q_G as the full subgroupoid of Π_1 on a finite set of symmetric base points
ideas.modern_name: fundamental groupoid with several base points; Teichmüller groupoid / Lego with basepoints at maximally degenerate curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme) for the idea; Ihara, Deligne (tangential basepoints); Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Moore–Seiberg for presentations
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), sections on the Teichmüller tower and groupoids based at 'points base' — only in general form, not this construction

missed.claim: Grothendieck intends an explicit generators-and-relations presentation of the local groupoid S_0T^Q_G at symmetric configurations (including J_I, J_II, J_III edge types and the ω_Q twist). He defers it ('j'y reviendrai'). Base points come from symmetry-induced ±1-torsors, a finer and more equivariant choice than the usual Lego basepoints.
missed.quote: Il faudra expliciter ce groupoïde basé en E_{G,Q} par générateurs et relations – j'y reviendrai
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Published presentations of Teichmüller groupoids (HLS, Bakalov–Kirillov, Funar–Gelca) use non-symmetric basepoints. A symmetry-adapted, equivariant version could bear on Galois/GT actions restricted to orbifold or symmetric strata. This is modest; it is likely recoverable by specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but essentially routine torsor bookkeeping step in Grothendieck's program of Teichmüller groupoids with canonical basepoints. The idea of symmetric 2-torsor basepoints is a nice unpublished detail, but it is not a striking result absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The opening word is probably 'Reprenant les précédentes définitions de', not 'prenant'.
Read 'Ceci posé, on aura' rather than 'on a[?], on aura'.
Read 'on peut poser pour simplifier' rather than 'poser par[?] simplifier[?]'.
Read 'faisant l'économie des facteurs ω_Q, nous avons' (the struck word precedes 'nous').
Read 'et on conserve l'expression ci-dessus pour SP^Y_G'; 'en conclut' looks unlikely.
The final sentence reads 'Il faudra expliciter ce groupoïde [-fondamental-] basé en E_{G,Q} par générateurs et relations – j'y reviendrai', not 'De façon explicite...'.
The diagram is {±1} → U^{J_I}, factored as diag: {±1} → {±1}^{J_I} followed by the canonical inclusion ('incl. can.').
